findings.text: Public tracking hooks for ordinary, per-cpu and vmalloc allocations only act when the global enabled flag is set and the supplied address is present and not an error encoding. Ordinary allocation records caller supplied size and minimum threshold, per-cpu records unit threshold, and vmalloc records the mapped address with threshold two plus an excess link from descriptor to mapping.

Partial free, ignore, no-scan, scan-area, transient and trace-refresh hooks share the same enabled and pointer validity gate, with scan-area additionally requiring nonzero length. They delegate respectively to partial deletion, blackening, disabling scanning of an object, registering an extra scannable interval, refreshing the content hash baseline, and replacing the stored stack identifier under the object lock.

Disabling scanning looks up the object without creating it. When absent it emits a warning mentioning the address and returns, otherwise it sets the no-scan marker while holding the object lock and then releases the acquired reference.

Content change detection refuses physical objects, suspends sanitizer tracking while reading, and recomputes a redundancy value over the whole extent, aggregating across every possible processor for per-cpu objects from a zero seed and otherwise over the untagged address. It reports whether the new value differs from the stored one.

Reference accounting applies only to white objects. Each discovered reference increments a counter and when the gray threshold derived from the minimum is reached a suspect marker is cleared with the global suspect tally decremented, a reference is retained, and the object is queued at the tail of the gray work list.

Pointer discovery strips address tags then discards values outside the tracked interval for the domain being scanned, using per-cpu bounds for per-cpu scans and global bounds otherwise. It ignores misses and references from an object to itself, passes only surplus references onward when the target is already gray, and forwards a stored excess link to a second object while ignoring circular links back to the scanned object.

Per-object state including flags, counts, hashes, trace identifiers and excess links is mutated under that object spinlock with interrupts managed, using a nested acquisition level when one object lock is taken while scanning holds another. The global tracking lock is held across the inner pointer walk so lookups need no extra reference, while the global scan mutex encloses whole scans and serializes writers to the reporting deduplication table.

Yielding while walking the object list first retains a reference, then under the global lock marks the object undeletable unless already removed, drops both the RCU read section and the lock to yield at a quiescent point, rejoins RCU and the lock, unlinks if removal was requested meanwhile, clears the marker, and finally releases the reference.

A tracked allocation record carries a base address, length, live reference count, required minimum, flag word, content hash, stack identifier, surplus link, use count, deletion state, duplicate tally, consecutive unreferenced scan tally, linkage for global list, interval membership, gray work queue, and a list of explicit scan intervals, plus its own spinlock.

An explicit scannable subrange carries a start address and length and is chained on its owning object. Objects with an empty chain or with the full-scan marker are examined over their entire extent instead of walking the chain.

A full pass whitens every object by zeroing counts, resets per-scan suspect marks, restarts unreferenced run lengths for nonwhite objects, paints out-of-range low-memory-external physical objects black, and seeds the gray queue from already gray ones. It then scans per-cpu sections, in-use pages of populated zones under the online-memory read guard with zone-ownership filtering, and optionally task stacks, drains the gray queue, re-queues white allocated objects whose content changed, flags remaining unreferenced unreported ones as suspects, and drains again.

Reporting runs a full pass to collect suspects and returns early when none remain or a stop was requested, then runs a confirmation pass that only refreshes references without marking changed objects. It walks the list a final time, promotes objects satisfying the unreferenced, suspect, unreported and age threshold to reported while counting them, deduplicates verbose output by stack identifier outside the object lock, flushes one entry per unique trace with a coalesced remainder note, and sets the global found flag.

Scanning stops promptly when the feature is disabled, when the background thread is asked to stop, or when a foreground caller has a pending signal. Large extents are divided into bounded chunks with scheduling quiescent points between chunks, and page walks additionally yield periodically; per-slot stop checks can truncate a block early.

The automatic scanner runs as a named kernel thread at lowered priority, optionally delaying the first iteration to let boot complete, then looping scan under the scan mutex followed by an interruptible sleep for a configurable interval until stopped.
Starting the scanner is idempotent when already running and clears the handle with a warning if thread creation fails. Stopping terminates and clears an existing thread and does nothing otherwise.

Debug listing iteration acquires the scan mutex interruptibly and holds an RCU read section across the walk, skipping to the requested offset and retaining the first live object, advancing with continue-from-cursor lookup while releasing the previous cursor, and on stop releasing RCU, the mutex and the final cursor. An interrupted lock acquisition yields an error pointer and releases nothing.

Color checks outside locks are intentionally racy to save overhead with misses deferred to the next pass. Concurrent reference motion can hide a live object for one pass, which the confirmation pass suppresses. Self and circular links are ignored, torn-down objects are skipped when retention fails, and task stack scanning is a possible source of missed references.

Scanning an object holds its lock so deletion cannot free the extent mid-read, revalidating allocation after each chunk where the lock was dropped for scheduling. Printing holds the object lock only around formatting and decides detailed dumping from the allocated marker, while deduplication insertion happens after unlocking to avoid nesting allocator locks inside the object spinlock.
Zone page scanning is enclosed by a paired online-memory read hold and release that brackets the whole zone loop.

Records without a stack identifier, including early boot allocations and depot failures, bypass deduplication and print immediately with full detail. Deduplication table insertion failures also fall back to immediate detailed printing, and successful unique entries print without detail when coalesced but with detail when solitary.
